comment: Two preference problems before the science even gets a turn. First, preferences.json is defaulted — the user has not told us anything about geography, travel tolerance, or willingness to relocate care, and PEMIGIST is a 24-patient single-site cohort at DFCI in Boston. Ranking that as the top contingency for a patient whose home address we do not know commits the user to a logistics burden they were never asked about. Second, the toxicity counseling is thin. Pemigatinib and the FGFR-inhibitor class carry serous retinal detachment in roughly a quarter of treated patients plus hyperphosphatemia that needs chronic monitoring. None of that shows up in the rationale. The patient deserves explicit AE counseling on any ranked option, and a low-confidence trial pick with single-PDX preclinical evidence is the place where that counseling matters most. Before this lands as rank 1, a real preferences elicitation has to happen and the AE profile has to be on the page.

The mechanism case for belzutifan is the cleanest in the dossier and 14 US sites is genuinely a better geography story than PEMIGIST. The qualified flag is about toxicity counseling that the rationale gestures at but does not actually do. This patient is post-gastrectomy with Roux-en-Y reconstruction and ECOG 1, and the belzutifan dataset shows hypoxia and anemia at the EPO-suppression target in roughly a quarter to a third of treated patients. Baseline-anemia management gets harder in a Roux-en-Y patient, and that needs to be on the consent form, not in the primary_concerns column. Preferences are defaulted, the user has not weighed in on chronic-monitoring tolerance, and the wt-GIST cohort still has no published readout. A real preferences conversation needs to happen before the patient signs.

Surveillance is the right baseline and the toxicity math gets there cleanly. What pulls a qualified rather than an endorse: the surveillance package itself is framed too passively. The preferences default is trials-preferring, and conservative's own rank 4 (Signatera) and rank 2 (NCI registry) are exactly the proactive pieces that turn 'structured surveillance' into something the user can feel they are doing rather than waiting for. The way the picks read now, those land as separate adjuncts; the preference-respecting move is to bundle them — registry enrollment plus paraganglioma screen plus Signatera baseline plus imaging cadence all read as one active-surveillance plan. The other flag: preferences.json is defaulted. A real elicitation has to happen before anyone commits the user to indefinite scan-based follow-up, because the soft cost of scan anxiety is a real preference axis nobody has asked about yet.

The contingency framing is right and the explicit 'not adjuvant today' language is the kind of discipline that protects the patient downstream. Where the pick underweights the defaulted preferences: trials-preferring is set to true, and at recurrence the sunitinib path should be presented alongside the trial route (PEMIGIST, LITESPARK-015 wt-GIST cohort, NCT05661643 temozolomide), not ahead of it as the default 2L. Boikos 18% ORR is the empirical anchor for choosing sunitinib over imatinib, but it is not a strong enough efficacy signal to outrank a trial slot on a defaulted trials-preferring preference set. AE counseling on the rationale is solid — fatigue, HFSR, hypothyroidism, hypertension all named — which is what the other contingency picks in this board are missing.

The evidence reasoning here lines up with the patient-preference read cleanly. No adjuvant therapy has efficacy in this molecular subset, the toxicity side of a defaulted 0.65 efficacy/toxicity weight wins by default when there is no efficacy signal to lean on, and the paraganglioma-screening pairing is the patient-safety floor that the surveillance plan needs. One note worth carrying into round 2: critic should also flag explicitly that preferences.json is defaulted, because the strength of this recommendation rests on the user not having stated a preference for 'doing something' over 'doing the right thing,' and that gap has to be closed before the recommendation hardens.

Same flag as on conservative's rank 3. Critic correctly identifies sunitinib as the only registration-grade systemic option in the contingency stack, and the AE-profile language is appropriately calibrated. The preference-fit issue is that prefers_trials defaults to true in this case, and ranking sunitinib at 3 while pushing belzutifan and pemigatinib and temozolomide all into 'trial-watch' tier underweights the user's defaulted trial preference at the moment of recurrence. At first measurable relapse, the trial-route options should be evaluated alongside sunitinib, not sequenced after it. The evidence quality argument that registration-grade beats trial-watch is correct on its own terms, but the defaulted preference set explicitly raises the bar for the trial side.

Endorse without qualification. The SDHB-intact / SDHA-biallelic paradox is exactly the kind of unresolved diagnostic flag that gets a patient bounced at trial screening, and critic's framing of the IHC re-stain plus germline SDHA closure plus tissue NGS confirmation as a prerequisite is the right discipline. From the patient-preference seat: this is also the highest-yield zero-toxicity move on any persona's list — it costs the patient nothing and unlocks every downstream option. Picking up the SDHC promoter methylation fallback in the same diagnostic pass is the move conservative and concensusite gestured at but did not anchor as firmly.

Guideline-perfect ranking that misreads the defaulted preference set. prefers_trials is true in preferences.json, and putting regorafenib at rank 4 ahead of the trial-route options (rank 5 temozolomide, with belzutifan and pemigatinib bundled inside that pick) sequences a registration-grade TKI ahead of the patient's defaulted trial preference. By the time this patient progresses on sunitinib, the dSDH-GIST trial landscape will likely have moved (concensusite's own rationale notes this) and the right move at 3L should be a fresh trial-landscape review, not a rotation to a TKI whose dSDH-GIST efficacy is by extrapolation. The AE-counseling note on hand-foot and hypertension is good. The preference-fit problem is the sequencing.

Cross-society convergence on surveillance is the cleanest read in this case and the chart-note discipline of citing ESMO plus Boikos 2016 so the decision does not get re-litigated is exactly right for protecting the patient downstream. One thing concensusite should add: the recommendation is anchored on a defaulted preferences.json. A real elicitation has to happen before this becomes the operative plan, and the chart note that documents the no-imatinib decision should also document that the user has not yet weighed in on scan-frequency tolerance, geography, or trial willingness. Otherwise solid.

Bundling three trials into a single rank-5 pick (NCT05661643 temozolomide, NCT04924075 belzutifan, NCT07434843 pemigatinib) collapses real geography differences that matter for a patient whose location is unknown. Asan is Korea-only, PEMIGIST is DFCI-only, LITESPARK-015 has 14 US sites — those are three different feasibility stories and they should not share a rank. The qualified flag is also about toxicity: temozolomide's MDS/AML long-tail at cumulative exposure, belzutifan's hypoxia/anemia in a post-Roux-en-Y patient, and pemigatinib's serous retinal detachment risk all deserve explicit counseling that the bundled rationale does not deliver. preferences.json is defaulted, so a trial-route at recurrence is preference-aligned, but the user needs to see the three trials as three different decisions with three different AE profiles and three different geography costs.

Mechanism work is interesting and I am not vetoing. The pick is queued for first recurrence, not started today, which is the right discipline. What I want on the record is the chronic-toxicity follow-up gap. NCT07434843 opened April 2026, so there is essentially no on-target chronic-exposure data in dSDH-GIST yet, and the FGFR-inhibitor class signal from the pemigatinib cholangiocarcinoma program (FIGHT-202) plus the infigratinib bladder program is real: serous retinal detachment in roughly a quarter of treated patients with cumulative exposure, hyperphosphatemia approaching 60% all-grade with phosphate-binder management, nail and mucosal toxicity that drives dose holds. Those are characterized AEs with management algorithms, but they require monthly OCT, weekly phosphate during titration, and a dermatology partner. That is a real chronic-monitoring burden for an oral targeted agent that will be running while the trial cohort is still establishing its dSDH-specific safety denominator. The 24-patient single-site phase-2 will not generate a long-tail safety dataset on the timescale a non-trial off-label decision would need. Conditional ask for the contingency note: if the patient recurs and this is the pick, the consent conversation has to name retinal toxicity and phosphate management specifically, and OCT baseline plus monthly OCT through the first 6 months has to be in the order set.

Mechanism is the cleanest in the dossier and the PPGL adjacency is real. Two safety points the rank-2 framing underweights. First, belzutifan has carried FDA approval since August 2021, so post-marketing surveillance is in the roughly 5-year window, at the low end of what I consider adequate long-tail follow-up for a chronic oral. Hypoxia and anemia are dose-limiting in roughly 25-30% of treated patients in the broader dataset. This patient is ECOG 1 post-gastrectomy with Roux-en-Y reconstruction, which compounds the anemia-management problem: iron and B12 absorption are already compromised, and EPO suppression on top of that is a stacked hit. Second, the wt-GIST cohort of LITESPARK-015 has not actually read out, so the bet rides on cross-tumor mechanism transport. That is a legitimate risktaker move, but the safety side cannot be borrowed from the PPGL cohort wholesale, because Roux-en-Y patients were not the registration population. Not a veto because the pick is contingency-only for measurable recurrence, but the consent and the iron/B12/Hgb baseline have to be locked before enrollment, and a Hgb floor for dose-hold needs to be in the protocol-deviation conversation.

Dissenting on toxicity and evidence quality both. The Sulkowski 2018 and Sulkowski 2020 mechanism work is genuinely tight, and the risktaker placed this at rank 4 rather than rank 1, which I respect. But for the conservative seat the combination has two non-trivial chronic-toxicity signals that the n=1 Singh 2023 case report cannot adjudicate. Overlapping cytopenias from PARP-trapping plus alkylator are not just additive in published combination data: OlympiA-style olaparib AML/MDS rates of approximately 1.2% rise sharply when the partner is itself genotoxic, and temozolomide carries its own roughly 1% MDS/AML long-tail at cumulative exposure beyond 6-12 months. The two together in a sustained-response scenario is exactly the chronic exposure where the MDS/AML signal compounds, and we have no published combination safety dataset in dSDH-GIST to anchor a management algorithm. Conditional veto if this is reached for: off-label PARP-plus-alkylator in dSDH-GIST without an active trial structure, without baseline marrow assessment, and without a pre-specified cumulative-exposure stopping rule is not something I can sign onto. Acceptable framing is 'late-line, trial-route only, with hematology co-management,' which is roughly where the risktaker landed. I want the framing tightened from 'post-trial-exhaustion contingency' to 'post-trial-exhaustion only, never as an off-label cash-pay default.'

I have the same pick at rank 4 of my own list, so the modality itself is not the disagreement. The disagreement is framing. The risktaker rationale describes the goal as 'compress lead time to action' so that 'contingency picks above can be triggered at first molecular relapse rather than waiting for RECIST-measurable disease.' That is exactly the use case the prospective validation data do not yet support in GIST. The colorectal and lung tumor-informed MRD literature establishes prognostic informativeness, not therapeutic actionability, and the GIST-specific dataset is even thinner. A ctDNA-positive / imaging-negative result in this patient should not trigger pemigatinib, belzutifan, sunitinib, or any other systemic agent. Full stop. The risktaker pick acknowledges this in the primary_concerns block but the rationale prose reads the other way, and the framing visible to the PI and the downstream chart is the rationale, not the concerns. Conditional ask, same guardrail I would put on any version of this pick: a positive Signatera result prompts shortened-interval imaging (CT or MRI at 6-8 weeks instead of the next q3-6 mo slot), not systemic therapy initiation. With that guardrail I agree the modality is worth running. Without it, a positive Signatera result becomes a pretext for early TKI and we have committed the NED patient to chronic toxicity on a non-validated trigger.

Full agreement on the call and on the evidence ladder behind it. The critic's RoB2:Low framing for Z9001, SSGXVIII, and PERSIST-5 paired with the structural-exclusion argument for dSDH-GIST is the cleanest articulation in the round-1 set of why those adjuvant trials do not transport. I would add the safety-side note the critic correctly held back from: even if the imatinib adjuvant data did transport, the AE profile on 3-year exposure (G3+ neutropenia approximately 4%, G2+ edema approximately 30%, fatigue approximately 50%, plus the unquantified long-tail of cardiac and hepatic monitoring burden) would still fail the NED-patient toxicity threshold at a 2% PR rate. The evidence and the safety side converge on the same answer, which is the cleanest decision in the dossier.

Agree on the call and on the internal-inconsistency argument. The biallelic-SDHA-inactivation-with-retained-SDHB pattern is the kind of finding that gets the patient bounced at trial screening, and resolving it now costs nothing beyond the re-cut and the germline panel. The critic's framing on the ctDNA-only variants (PIK3CA R93W outside the alpelisib hotspots per Burke 2012, MAP2K1 P124S not yet tissue-confirmed) is also the right discipline. From the safety seat: every dollar of chronic-toxicity exposure that gets averted by NOT anchoring a PI3Kα or MEK inhibitor on an unconfirmed ctDNA-only driver call is a clean win, and the alpelisib AE profile (G3+ hyperglycemia approximately 37%, G3+ rash approximately 10%, pneumonitis signal) is precisely the kind of chronic burden that should not be committed on weak driver evidence.

Same pick as my own rank 3, same contingency framing. One safety-side amplification: the critic's concern that 'characteristic sunitinib toxicity is well-characterized but not benign on the indolent natural history of this subtype' is the load-bearing point and it deserves more weight than the round-1 rationale gave it. dSDH-GIST patients are often younger (median age in the high-yield series is mid-30s) and tend to need multi-year TKI exposure if they respond. Cumulative hypothyroidism, sustained hand-foot, chronic hypertension, and the cardiac LVEF signal at prolonged dosing are real, and they accrue on the natural-history timescale of this disease. Sunitinib at first measurable recurrence is the right call. Sunitinib started early on a ctDNA-only signal, or out of recurrence anxiety, is the wrong one, and the contingency note should say so explicitly.

Agree on the call and on the cross-society convergence framing. NCCN GIST v1.2025 plus ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2022 plus the natural-history anchor from Mei 2018 is the cleanest guideline-fit case in the round-1 set. The concensusite's third primary_concern (the chart note should cite ESMO 2022 and Boikos 2016 so the decision is documented and not re-litigated) is a particularly good operational discipline and I want it on the record from the safety seat too: the most likely failure mode here is a community oncologist downstream reaching for adjuvant imatinib on reflex, and a clearly documented dissent in the chart is the cheapest insurance against that.

Agree on the pick and on the 'NOT adjuvant' framing in the intervention label, which is the right discipline. One operational note from the safety seat: the concensusite is correct that 37.5 mg continuous is often better tolerated than 50 mg 4-on/2-off in this subset, and I would push that observation a step further. For dSDH-GIST patients on multi-year TKI exposure, the published practice (Mavroeidis 2025, Dedousis 2025) is to plan for dose modification to 37.5 mg continuous within the first 2-3 cycles as the rule rather than the exception. Building that into the contingency note as the anticipated trajectory (rather than treating it as a failure of label dosing) preserves treatment continuity when the AE conversation gets to the prescribing oncologist.

I have temozolomide at my own rank 5 with similar framing, so the pick itself is not the disagreement. What I want sharpened is the chronic-exposure safety conversation. The Yebra 2022 protocol uses low-dose continuous TMZ for sustained periods, and the MDS/AML long-tail at approximately 1% with cumulative TMZ exposure beyond 6-12 months is the chronic signal that the round-1 concensusite rationale does not name. For a dSDH-GIST patient who may respond and stay on for years, that signal accrues on the natural-history timescale of the disease and is not adequately characterized in an n=5 mini-cohort. Conditional ask: if the patient reaches this pick, MGMT methylation has to be confirmed on archival block first to enrich the response-probability case, baseline CBC and marrow reserve documented, and a pre-specified cumulative-exposure re-evaluation point (somewhere in the 9-12 month range) written into the plan. With those guardrails I agree the trial-route framing is the right one and the pick stays in the contingency stack.

Agree on the call. The advocate's framing that 'none of [the contingency picks] is reachable later if we burn a year of TKI toxicity now' is the right way to put the option-preservation argument to a patient, and it captures something the more technical guideline-fit framing does not. Starting an adjuvant TKI that the molecular evidence already rejects does not just expose the patient to AEs, it also burns the screening eligibility for several of the trial picks, because most require measurable disease and would deprioritize a screen-failed prior-systemic-therapy patient. The toxicity-side argument and the option-preservation argument converge on the same answer.

The diagnostic-bundle framing is right and the one-tissue-pull-three-answers operational discipline is exactly what should happen. My qualification is on the Signatera baseline inclusion in this bundle. The advocate's rationale describes the ctDNA result as something that 'could legitimately move the conversation from surveillance to sunitinib before the patient is symptomatic.' That phrasing reads to me like the ctDNA-as-actionable framing that the prospective validation data do not yet support in GIST. A tumor-informed MRD assay is informative for prognosis and lead time. It is not yet a validated trigger for systemic therapy initiation in NED dSDH-GIST. Conditional ask, same guardrail I asked of the risktaker: a positive Signatera result prompts shortened-interval imaging (CT or MRI at 6-8 weeks), not sunitinib initiation. With that explicit in the chart, the baseline build is worth doing on the same tissue pull. Without it, the assay becomes an anxiety amplifier with a TKI-initiation footgun attached.

Strong agreement on the explicit dissent listing. Putting adjuvant imatinib on the picks list specifically to mark it NOT-recommended is a discipline I want amplified. The most likely failure mode in the downstream care path is exactly the 'GIST equals imatinib' reflex the advocate names, and a documented veto in the structured output is the cheapest insurance against it. From the safety seat I will add my own veto to the record here: any subsequent recommendation in this case that initiates adjuvant imatinib (or any adjuvant systemic therapy) in this NED dSDH-GIST patient draws an unconditional veto from me. The 2% PR rate in Boikos 2016 against the imatinib AE profile (G2+ edema approximately 30%, fatigue approximately 50%, hepatic and cardiac monitoring burden over 3-year exposure) is not a defensible toxicity tradeoff at any reasonable efficacy/toxicity weighting, and the structural exclusion of dSDH-GIST from Z9001, SSGXVIII, and PERSIST-5 means there is no transportable adjuvant benefit signal to weigh against the AE side at all.

The pyramid is too narrow to anchor a rank-1 pick. One PDX model from Flynn 2025 (AACR abstract CT215, not peer-reviewed at full-paper resolution) plus a rogaratinib sister-drug readout at n=24 with ORR 41.7%, exact binomial 95% CI roughly 22-63%, plus a 24-patient single-arm phase-2 at one site. That is mechanistic plausibility plus a small unreplicated signal, not the strongest preclinical-to-clinic translation in dSDH-GIST. The rationale calls it that and overstates what the evidence supports. The class FGFRi toxicity (serous retinal detachment around 25%, hyperphosphatemia) is also missing from the framing. Track the readout; do not anchor a contingency plan on it.

Mechanism is the cleanest in the dossier and 14 US sites is a real practical advantage. The problem is the effect estimate the rationale is implicitly transporting. PPGL ORR 26%, mPFS 22 mo is a fair adjacency on succinate-HIF-2 biology, but a 26% PPGL number does not transport to GIST as a quantitative expectation. LITESPARK-015 is single-arm open-label phase 2 with ORR as the primary endpoint, so a positive readout will not generate OS data and no comparator will exist. Watch-item with caveats, not a tied-second pick.

Yebra 2022 is n=5 with no comparator. The exact binomial 95% CI on 2/5 PR runs roughly 5% to 85%. That is not a 40% ORR estimate; it is an interval that contains essentially the entire range from inactive to highly active. ROBINS-I rates the clinical cohort serious because response capture is retrospective on a small selected sample paired with PDX modeling. The rationale invokes 100% DCR as if it has meaning at n=5 in an indolent natural-history setting, and the closest mechanism-coherent precedent (Ligon 2023 guadecitabine, 0/9 across cohorts) is the cautionary readout the rationale brushes past. Wait for NCT03556384 (UCSD, active-not-recruiting, primary completion June 2025) before treating 2/5 as actionable.

The Sulkowski 2018 and 2020 mechanism work is real and tight on the SDH/FH-loss synthetic-lethal logic. Human clinical evidence in dSDH-GIST is one patient (Singh 2023, letter-format case report, no abstract), which is the weakest cell in the evidence table. The rationale labels this honestly as the weakest rank, so this is not a veto. The flag is that the n=1 caveat needs to travel forward into any board-level recommendation language so it does not get cited as 'durable response in dSDH-GIST' down the line. Mechanistic plausibility without clinical confirmation does not move my prior, and overlapping PARP + alkylator cytopenias make this a real-tolerability regimen at the point of late-line use.

MRD as a lead-time signal is reasonable. What is not reasonable is the framing that a ctDNA-positive result could compress lead-time-to-action on a trial slot. The patient's ctDNA-only variants in the dossier (PIK3CA R93W, MAP2K1 P124S, SDHA E350fs not seen on tumor NGS) are exactly the kind of low-VAF plasma calls that need tissue confirmation before they are treated as drivers. R93W is not on the validated alpelisib companion-diagnostic panel, and Burke 2012 biochemistry classifies the ABD-domain class as weakly activating. Using Signatera positivity to push the patient toward trial enrollment before measurable disease is treating noise as signal. Imaging confirmation must gate any systemic-therapy decision.

Agreed on the contingency framing and the imatinib-skip logic. The push-back: the rationale leans on 7/38 (18%) ORR from Boikos 2016 without flagging that the retrospective subgroup carries no confidence interval and ROBINS-I rates the cohort moderate. Demetri 2006 is RoB2:Low and registration-grade for KIT-mutant 2L GIST, but the dSDH subset in the pivotal phase 3 is minimally represented, so the activity claim in this molecular subtype runs through Boikos as an indication-extrapolation argument, not a subset-of-the-RCT argument. The 18% number is directional. The chart note should say so.

Registry enrollment is the right move and the SDHA germline question is correctly elevated. What I want pushed harder than the rationale does: the SDHB-intact / SDHA-biallelic discrepancy is not a footnote, it is a structural threat to the dSDH-GIST label itself. Biallelic SDHA loss at combined VAF around 85% should destabilize the complex and abolish SDHB staining. The rationale notes an SDHB re-stain and an SDHA IHC but lists it as one of several diagnostic loose ends. It is the loose end. Every dSDH-GIST trial in this dossier (NCT04924075, NCT05661643, NCT07434843) uses SDHB-IHC loss as the entry phenotype. If SDHB is genuinely retained after a clean re-stain with documented positive internal control, this case becomes a molecularly-SDH-deficient / immunohistochemically-SDH-proficient outlier and trial-screener eligibility collapses.

Agreed on rank-5 framing and the explicit acknowledgement that Yebra 2022 n=5 plus PDX work is the load-bearing clinical evidence, with Ligon 2023 guadecitabine 0/9 as the cautionary precedent. Right framing of pending phase-2 readouts. The MGMT-methylation-on-archival call now is the correct operational move regardless of whether TMZ ever enters the plan.

NCCN endorsement is real and Demetri 2006 is RoB2:Low. The rationale stops one step short of what the evidence actually supports: NCCN's 2L preference for sunitinib in KIT/PDGFRA-WT GIST is itself anchored on Boikos 2016 retrospective n=38 (7/38, 18% ORR, no CI, ROBINS-I:Moderate), because the registration cohort had minimal dSDH-GIST representation. Cross-society endorsement does not upgrade the underlying subset evidence to RCT-level. NCCN category 2A built on a retrospective n=38 subgroup is expert consensus on the best available evidence, not category 1.

GRID is RoB2:Low (PFS HR 0.27, 95% CI 0.19-0.39) and the 3L positioning is correct. The rationale gets the framing right when it calls dSDH-GIST activity an extrapolation. What I would add: GRID enrolled essentially no dSDH-GIST patients, and the Dedousis 2025 review's 'modest activity, similar to KIT-mutant 3L' claim is qualitative narrative, not a published subset analysis with a confidence interval. Defensible as a contingency anchor because the 3L alternatives are thinner. The evidence pyramid for regorafenib in this molecular subtype is RCT-in-different-population plus expert-narrative, not RCT-in-population.

Cross-society convergence (NCCN GIST v1.2025, ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2022) on no adjuvant TKI in resected dSDH-GIST is genuinely strong, and the Z9001 / SSGXVIII / PERSIST-5 population-mismatch logic is correctly framed. The sharpening point: the SDHB-intact / SDHA-biallelic phenotype discrepancy noted in primary_concerns is structurally more important than the rationale implies. The dSDH label is the load-bearing assumption under the entire surveillance recommendation. If the phenotype does not lock in after the re-stain, the case turns into something else. Worth elevating in the round-2 board synthesis rather than listing.

Trial-route framing is correct and the honest acknowledgement that Yebra n=5 is not category-1 evidence is the right disposition for a guideline persona. What I would add: even the 40% ORR signal should travel with its 95% CI (roughly 5-85% by exact method) attached, because at n=5 the point estimate is uninformative without the interval. The MGMT-methylation-at-recurrence sequencing is the right operational call.

Agreed on contingency framing and on the explicit NED-now-not-later positioning. The 18% versus 2% comparison from Boikos 2016 is the right qualitative anchor for choosing sunitinib over imatinib at 2L, but the rationale should attach a 'directional, not precise' caveat because the dSDH subset is n=38 retrospective with no confidence interval. Demetri 2006 RoB2:Low does not extend to the dSDH subgroup; subset transportability is a ROBINS-I axis the rationale skips.

Best-framed pick on the board for this issue. Germline SDHA resolution plus SDHA/SDHB IHC re-cut plus tissue confirmation of the ctDNA-only PIK3CA R93W and MAP2K1 P124S calls is the right one-tissue-pull, three-answers operational move. Framing ctDNA as informative-not-actionable, and the IHC discordance as a trial-screener gate rather than a footnote, is the strongest in the round. The only push: SDHB-intact alongside biallelic SDHA inactivation at combined VAF around 85% is genuinely paradoxical at the protein-stability level. If the re-stain confirms retained SDHB, the whole dSDH label is in play and the trial portfolio narrows fast.

Worth listing the dissent on the record. Boikos 2016 1/49 (2%) PR is the published anchor, and the ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS 2022 recommendation is explicit. The Z9001 / SSGXVIII / PERSIST-5 population-mismatch argument is structurally correct because dSDH-GIST was not a recognized subtype at the time those trials accrued. PERSIST-5 separating out the imatinib-insensitive genotypes and showing they recur on or off treatment is the cleanest single demonstration that dSDH-GIST belongs in the imatinib-insensitive class. No quarrel from the evidence-quality seat.
